data.definition: The target suffers a −X Modifier to its Evade Rolls against this attack.
This weapon can't make a Ranged Attack while its Unit is Engaged.
Against a target Within Y″ of the attacking model, the weapon's RoA goes up by X for that attack.

Artefact Hunt rules. A Unit CLAIMS a Mission Marker by putting it on its Unit Card, and can carry only one at a time. It must DROP the Marker if its Current Supply Value drops, before it resolves a PLACE effect, if it's Engaged with Enemies of greater combined Current Supply, or if it's Destroyed, removed or returned to Reserves. The opponent then sets the Marker Within 2″ of the Unit (or its last model).
An attack with this weapon can remove at most X models. Any Damage left after that is discarded, not recorded on a Damage Marker.
Move up to X dice from the Armour Pool straight into the Damage Pool, skipping the Armour Roll. It can't move more dice than are in the Armour Pool.

The Unit improves a characteristic by X until the End of the Round. For a Target Number (Armour, Hit) that means lower and easier to roll; for a value (Speed, RoA) it means higher. Tracked with a blue Marker.
The Unit worsens a characteristic by X until the End of the Round. A Target Number goes up (harder to roll); a value goes down (minimum 0). Tracked with a red Marker.

A Leading Model may end a move overlapping this Token or model. If it does, the controlling player immediately sets the displaced piece in base contact with the Leading Model (or as close as possible).
When this Unit is attacked, Surge and CRITICAL HIT move X fewer dice from the Armour Pool to the Damage Pool (minimum 0).
Remove X points of Damage from the Unit's Damage Marker. It can't bring back Destroyed models (that's RESPAWN) and can't restore Shielded.
The Unit takes X automatic hits: put X dice straight into its Armour Pool with Damage Y and go to Armour Rolls. These hits never generate Surge.

Right after a successful Charge, each model in the Fighting or Supporting Rank rolls X Impact dice at the Enemy Unit(s) it's fighting (split between them if several). Each result of Y or more puts one die in that Unit's Armour Pool, with Damage 1 and no Surge. HIDDEN Units are immune.
This weapon may ignore Line of Sight when choosing and hitting a target (it still needs Range). A target that's out of Line of Sight gets an Evade Roll.
Enemy Units can't use Reaction abilities in response to attacks made with this weapon.
Ranged Attacks with this weapon get +X RoA against a target with the STATIONARY Status.
The weapon's maximum Range becomes X″. Models firing beyond the normal Range (but Within X″) suffer −1 to Hit; roll them separately from the rest of the Batch.

Needs enough Available Supply. Set one model of the named Unit in base contact with the active Unit, then remove X of the active Unit's models. The new Unit can't be set Within 1″ of an Enemy, and gets an Activation Marker: it can't activate for the rest of the Round.
Add X to the Unit's Damage Marker but don't remove any models, even if that exceeds a model's HP. The next normal Damage counts the total and removes casualties as usual.
A Ground Zerg Unit (Friendly or Enemy) is ON CREEP while Within 6″ of a Creep Tumor Token or a model that's a Source of Creep. Some abilities and upgrades only work while ON CREEP.
Against a Unit with the named Combat Tag, this weapon's Damage becomes X.
Ranged Attacks with this weapon may target Enemy Units that are Engaged, which is normally not allowed.

Pick up the Leading Model and set it Wholly Within X″ of where it started. It isn't moved along a path, so Gap Clearance and elevation don't matter. Then set the rest of the Unit In Coherency. It can't end Within Engagement Range of an Enemy, except in the Assault Phase (where the Unit becomes Engaged).
After rolling to Hit, move up to X failed dice into the Armour Pool. They count as hits for everything, including Surge.
This ability ignores the once-per-Round limit. Use it as often as you can pay its cost and meet its trigger, even several times in one Activation.
Return up to X Destroyed models to the Unit, each in base contact with a surviving model and not Within Engagement Range of an Enemy. It can't push the Unit into a higher Supply bracket.
Models may use this weapon on top of their normal weapon, ignoring the one-weapon-per-model rule. It's resolved as its own Batch, so it can pick a different target.
Only one model in the Unit may carry this weapon or upgrade. Other upgrades apply to every model.
Template hits on models outside the Primary target Unit. Each extra Unit is its own Batch, with no RoA modifiers and no Surge, and it can hit Friendly Units too.
This Token, Marker or effect survives Cleanup & Refresh and stays until something specifically removes it.

Set the named Unit's Leading Model in base contact with the Parent Unit and the rest In Coherency, not Within Engagement Range of an Enemy or in the opponent's Zone of Influence. Needs enough Available Supply. It can't activate in the Phase it arrived; after that it activates right after its Parent.
When this Unit makes Armour Rolls, turn up to X failures into successes.
A Status that Stukov's Forces put on Enemy Units (Spread Infestation, Parasitic Bio-Toxins). It counts as a DEBUFF, and many Stukov abilities and Virus Cards do extra things to Units that have it.

A mode (Status). The Unit also gains HIDDEN, counts as Size 0, counts as Supply 0 for Disengage checks, and can't Control or Contest Mission Markers. It may only Deploy, Move, Disengage, Run, Hold or Close Ranks, and all of those except Hold remove BURROWED. It gets an Evade Roll against every attack. Other models may move through it but not end Within its Engagement Range. If Engaged in the Combat Phase, it must Close Ranks (which unburrows it) to attack.
Can't be targeted by Ranged Attacks or Line of Sight abilities unless the attacker is Within 4″, and isn't Visible beyond 4″. Immune to IMPACT. Gets an Evade Roll against every attack.
A mode (Status). The Unit can't Move, Disengage, Run, Charge or Close Ranks. Only its SIEGE MODE weapons work, and those work only in this mode. Lost if the Unit returns to Reserves.
Every Unit gains this at the Start of the Round, and loses it as soon as any of its models moves, is moved or is PLACED.

A Unit with a Shield value adds it to its first model's HP and is Shielded. It stops being Shielded once its Total Damage exceeds the Shield value or the first model is removed. HEAL can't restore it.

A lasting condition or mode on a Unit (e.g. BURROWED, SIEGE MODE, BUFF). Statuses aren't cleared in Scoring & Cleanup unless a rule says so. Track modes with plastic Markers and other effects with blue (good) or red (bad) Markers.
The part of a terrain piece that connects elevation levels. Models move between levels through it.

In the Movement, Assault and Combat Phases, players take turns activating one Unit each. An activated Unit performs one action and gets an Activation Marker. (Mission Markers also have an "Activated" side; that's different.)
Placed next to a Unit once it has acted this Phase, so it can't activate again.

A deliberate ability. The Unit must be Activated, and you use it just before declaring an action or right after one finishes. Each named Active ability works once per Round per Unit (unless REPEATABLE), and its effects end at the End of the Round unless stated.
Always on while the Unit is on the battlefield. No decision needed. Off while in Reserves unless stated.

Used the moment its trigger happens (an attack, a Charge, a model Destroyed…), outside the normal turn order. Each player gets one Reaction per Activation, and each named Reaction works once per Round per Unit. If both players react to the same trigger, the Active Player goes first.
Your Supply Pool minus the Current Supply Value of your Units on the battlefield. A Unit can only Deploy from Reserves if its Current Supply Value fits. No limit in the final Round.
One group of attack dice resolved together (normally one weapon type against one target). SIDEARMS and Spillover are separate Batches.
Any terrain with an Effective Size of 1 or more. It can block Line of Sight under the Cover rules.

Assault Phase action. An Unengaged Ground Unit declares Ground targets (no Line of Sight needed), rolls a D6, and its Leading Model moves up to Speed plus the roll to end Engaged with them. Flying Units can't Charge or be Charged.
The Combat Phase attack. Only Engaged Units activate. Models in the Fighting and Supporting Ranks strike with their Combat Phase weapons.
Optional first step of a Close Combat Attack: move the Leading Model up to 3″ closer to the Enemies the Unit is Engaged with, then press models into base contact. It can't pull in new Enemy Units.

After any action that repositions a Unit, every model must be Wholly Within 3″ of the Leading Model, linked to it through a chain of its own models. Then the Unit is In Coherency. Casualties never break Coherency.

At the end of each Round, each player adds up the Current Supply of their Units Contesting a Mission Marker (on the battlefield, In Coherency, with a model Within 3″ and in Line of Sight of it on the same elevation). The higher total takes Control. Control is sticky: it stays until the opponent beats it, and ties change nothing. Flying, BURROWED and Reserve Units can't Contest.
A Zerg Token that spreads creep: Ground Zerg Units Within 6″ of it are ON CREEP.
A Unit's Supply right now, read from its Supply Profile for the models it has left. It drops as casualties push it into a lower bracket. Used for Deploying, Mission Marker Control and Tactical Mass.
Records Damage a Unit has taken that wasn't enough to remove another model. It adds to the next Damage the Unit takes.

Movement Phase action: a Unit in Reserves enters from your Entry Edge, moving up to its Speed. Its Current Supply Value must fit your Available Supply, and it can't end in the opponent's Zone of Influence.

How attacks resolve. Roll the Attack Pool to Hit; hits move to the Armour Pool. Surge may move some straight to the Damage Pool. The defender rolls the rest against Armour, and failures go to the Damage Pool. An eligible Unit then makes an Evade Roll. Each die left deals the weapon's Damage.

Movement Phase action for an Engaged Unit: move away using normal Move rules. Models that can't end outside every Enemy's Engagement Range are Destroyed; if the Leading Model can't, the Disengage fails and it's removed. Next Assault Phase the Unit can't Ranged Attack or Charge, unless it has Tactical Mass.
A model's Size plus the Size of the terrain it's standing on. It decides what blocks Line of Sight. Flying models count as taller than any terrain.

GROUND LEVEL is on the playmat, MID GROUND is on Size 1–2 terrain, and HIGH GROUND is on Size 3+ terrain. Models on HIGH GROUND and GROUND LEVEL can't Engage each other. MID GROUND can Engage either only across a shared ACCESS POINT.

A Ground Unit is Engaged when any of its models is Within 1″ of an Enemy Ground model, unless Size 2+ terrain or an elevation difference prevents it. Engaged Units can't Move (they Disengage or Hold) and have limits on Ranged Attacks. Flying Units are never Engaged.
1″ horizontally from a model's base. Melee weapons (Range E) only reach targets in it.
The table edge the Deployment Card gives you. Your Units Deploy from Reserves through it.
Only when a rule grants one, or when an Engaged Unit is hit by a Ranged Attack. The defender rolls the dice in the Damage Pool against the Unit's Evade. Each success cancels a die.
The defender rolls the dice in the Armour Pool against the Unit's Armour. Successes are discarded, and failures move to the Damage Pool.

Faction and Tactical Cards start each Round Ready (face up). Exhaust one (flip it face down) to use its own ability, or to generate its resource (CP, BM or PE) to pay a cost elsewhere. Excess resource is lost. Exhausted cards refresh in Cleanup.
The Fighting Rank is models Within 1″ of an Enemy. The Supporting Rank is models in base contact with a Fighting Rank model from their own Unit. Both strike in Close Combat and generate IMPACT dice.

Whoever holds it chooses who activates first each Phase. The first player to Pass in the Movement or Assault Phase takes it for the next Phase. At the end of the Round it goes to the player with fewer VP (Roll-Off if tied).
"D3+1" means roll and add 1. It's a value, not a Modifier to a Target Number.
The Unit does nothing this Activation and gets an Activation Marker.
Terrain with no ACCESS POINT to the next level. Models can't move through, onto or across it, or end on it. (Size 0 and 1 terrain can be moved through.)
For any move, you pick one model as the Leading Model, move it (measuring its path), then set the rest In Coherency around it.
Traced top-down from any part of one base to any part of the other. Terrain blocks it only under the Cover rules (Full Cover, Direct Cover, Elevation Dead Zone). It's always mutual.
Numbered Markers set out from the Deployment Card: 1 and 3 Red, 2 and 4 Blue, 5 Neutral. Each has an Activated and a Deactivated side. They're the main way to score.

Changes a roll's Target Number: +X makes it easier, −X harder. A Target Number never goes below 2+ or above 6+, a natural 6 always succeeds and a natural 1 always fails. Different named sources stack.
The Unit that SUMMONED another Unit. The summoned Unit activates right after it.

Instead of activating a Unit, a player may Pass, and must Pass with nothing left to activate. Once you've Passed you're done for that Phase. The first to Pass takes the First Player Marker for the next Phase.
Assault Phase action: an Unengaged Unit fires its Assault Phase weapons at a target in Range and Line of Sight. Engaged Units are restricted (see PINPOINT and BULKY).

Every Unit starts the game off the table in Reserves. Units there can't be targeted, can't use abilities (unless stated), and don't count toward your Supply on the battlefield. Units still in Reserves at the end of the final Round count as Destroyed for scoring.
Both players roll 2D6; the higher total wins, and ties roll again.
Each Round has four Phases: Movement, Assault, Combat, then Scoring & Cleanup. Effects "until the End of the Round" are cleared in Cleanup.
Assault Phase action: an Unengaged Unit moves up to its Speed instead of attacking.
The total Current Supply you may have on the battlefield this Round. It starts at the Mission's value and grows each Round, and is unlimited in the final Round.
A Unit's Supply from its Supply Profile. Its starting Supply Value (from the composition you bought) is how many Army Slots it fills.

Weapons with S Dice roll a Surge Die with their attack. If the target has the weapon's Surge Type tag, move that many dice from the Armour Pool straight to the Damage Pool, skipping Armour. Otherwise the Surge Die does nothing.

A Unit has Tactical Mass when its Current Supply Value is higher than the combined Current Supply of every Enemy Unit it's Engaged with. A Unit that Disengages with Tactical Mass may still Ranged Attack and Charge next Assault Phase.
Blast Template (BT) and Flamer Template (FT) weapons hit every model under the template at the target's elevation. Models outside the Primary target take Spillover.
A physical battlefield object (Creep Tumor, Corrosive Bile…). It's treated as Size 0 terrain: models move through it but can't end on it. Removed at the End of the Round unless stated.
Not Within 1″ of any Enemy Ground model (or terrain prevents Engagement). Only Unengaged Units can Move, Run, Charge or fire freely. Flying Units are always Unengaged.
Only one copy of this Unit or card may be in your army.
A model is Visible to another if there's a valid Line of Sight between them. Only Visible models can be removed as casualties from an attack.
Points scored from the Mission Card each Round. Most at the end wins; some Missions end early on a big enough lead.
A model is Within a distance if any part of its base is in range. A Unit is Within if at least one model is.
A model is Wholly Within a distance only if its entire base is in range. A Unit is Wholly Within only if every model is.
The 6″ strip in from each player's Entry Edge. Units arriving from Reserves (including by SUMMON or transport) can't end in the opponent's. It has no other effect.
Everything belonging to you (and teammates) is Friendly; everything of your opponent's is Enemy. You can't attack Friendly Units unless a rule says so.
Core, Elite, Support, Air and Hero. Your Faction Card gives some, and Tactical Cards add more. A Unit fills slots of its type equal to its starting Supply Value. Unused slots are lost.

Armoured, Biological, Light, Mechanical, Psionic, Flying and Ground. Weapons and abilities check them: Target, Surge Type, PIERCE and so on. Ground (the tag) isn't the same as GROUND LEVEL (an elevation).

A Combat Tag. Flying Units ignore terrain and elevation when moving, are never Engaged, can't Charge or be Charged, don't fight in the Combat Phase, and can't Control or Contest Mission Markers. For cover they count as taller than any terrain.
Race (Terran, Zerg, Protoss) and sub-faction tags (e.g. Raynor's Raiders). A Unit or Tactical Card is allowed only if every one of its tags is on your Faction Card.
Every army has exactly one. It sets your Faction Tags, gives your starting Army Slots and resource, and has its own abilities.
Bought with Vespene Gas. Each adds Army Slots, provides a resource when Exhausted, and has abilities. Zerg also take exactly one Creep card (Stukov's Forces: one Virus card instead).
Stukov's Forces' answer to the Creep card: the army takes exactly one, paying its gas cost. Each one adds an effect against INFESTATION-ed enemies plus the usual Creep Tumor rules.
Terran's resource for paying ability costs (e.g. "1 CP"). Generated by Exhausting a Ready Terran card.
Zerg's resource for paying ability costs (e.g. "1 BM"). Generated by Exhausting a Ready Zerg card.
Protoss's resource for paying ability costs (e.g. "1 PE"). Generated by Exhausting a Ready Protoss card.
Army-building budgets. Minerals buy Units and upgrades; Vespene Gas buys Tactical Cards. Skirmish is 1000 / 100 and Standard 2000 / 200.
How far (in inches) the Leading Model moves in a standard Move. With two values (e.g. 4/7), use the second if the Unit is down to one model or started with one. "-" means it can't move at all.
The Target Number the defender needs on a D6 to cancel a hit in the Armour Roll.
The Target Number for Evade Rolls, which a Unit only gets when a rule grants one. "-" means it can never Evade.
How much Damage one model takes before it's removed.
Extra HP added to the Unit's first model. The Unit is Shielded until that's used up.
A model's height category, used for Line of Sight and moving past terrain.
A weapon's maximum reach in inches. E means Engagement Range (melee). FT means a Flamer Template.
What a weapon can shoot: Ground, Flying, or All.
Dice each firing model rolls. BT+X means a Blast Template plus X.
The Target Number each attack die needs on a D6 to hit.
The Surge Die a weapon rolls (D3 or D6). No S Dice means no Surge.
Damage each die left in the Damage Pool deals.
